name: Answering Service Care
task: Someone — or an AI — to answer the calls we miss
summary: US-based live answering with real people, 24/7 and bilingual English/Spanish, with call transfers, SMS and email relays, a client portal and app on every plan.
best_for: a small business that loses money when a call goes to voicemail — trades, clinics, law and property firms — and wants real people answering around the clock without hiring a receptionist. It suits you especially if your call volume is genuinely low and predictable, because the plans are priced in minutes and nothing is gated behind a higher tier
skip_if: your callers mostly want things a human does not need to do — order status, opening hours, a password reset — because you are paying per minute for a person to read them out. Skip it too if your volume is high and variable: at 500-plus minutes you are past the published ladder and into a custom quote, and per-minute billing makes a busy month expensive in a way a flat-rate provider would not
honest_knock: Do the arithmetic before you pick a tier, because their own page does not. Starter buys the line and nothing else: at $40 plus $1.75 a minute, it stays the cheapest option only up to roughly 79 minutes a month — past that the $179 Small Business plan costs less. The same crossover logic repeats: Small Business gives way to Pro at about 188 minutes, and Pro gives way to Enterprise at about 444. Note too that Small Business is the one tier where an included minute ($1.79 each, $179 for 100) costs more than an overage minute ($1.70), so there is no saving in buying that bundle for its own sake. And the second thing to price in is the $50 start-up fee, which is easy to miss where they have put it.

pricing.notes: (2026-09-10, read off their own pricing page, both billing toggles) Four plans, priced on included minutes. Billed monthly: Starter $40 with zero minutes included and $1.75 per minute after that; Small Business $179 for 100 minutes, then $1.70; Pro $329 for 250 minutes, then $1.60; Enterprise $639 for 500 minutes, then $1.35. Paying a year upfront takes about 10% off the monthly rate: $161, $296 and $575 for the three larger plans, while Starter stays at $40. There is also a $50 one-time start-up fee; it is still absent from the plan cards, but the page's FAQ now says plainly what it buys — customising the account, building your initial scripts and configuring routing. Every plan carries the same feature set: 24/7 cover, bilingual English/Spanish operators, call transfers, SMS and email relays, custom greetings and hold music, a client portal, usage reporting and the mobile app. So you are buying minutes, not capability, and there is no long-term contract. One caution about the page itself: the explanatory text below the table still contradicts the table three times, quoting Pro at $319, Enterprise at $599 and Starter overage at $1.65. We have used the figures from the pricing table, which is the one the buttons act on.

compare_with.name: Ruby
compare_with.why: the best-known US answering service and the comparison most buyers will make. Both sell live, US-based receptionists on a minute bundle; the practical difference is where your volume sits against each ladder and what a spare minute costs when you go over. Answering Service Care's advantage is that every feature — bilingual operators, relays, the portal — is on every plan, so the tier you choose is purely a volume decision
